sentences.text: Pravusuchus is unique among phytosaurs because the lateral rim of its nostril is formed by the septomaxilla rather than the nasal bone.
The animal possesses alveolar ridges visible from the side, a trait it shares with some other phytosaurs but not with Smilosuchus gregorii or Pseudopalatus.
Its snout is partially crested but lacks a premaxillary crest.
The generic name Pravusuchus combines the Latin word for 'evil' or 'wicked' and the Greek name for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
The species name refers to the Devil's Playground locality within Petrified Forest National Park where fossils were found.
The genus Pravusuchus was first described by Stocker in 2010.
The type species of the genus is Pravusuchus hortus.
The specific name hortus means 'park' or 'grounds' in Latin.
The genus is known from three specimens: a mostly complete holotype skull and two referred partial skulls with additional fragments.
All known fossils of Pravusuchus come from the Sonsela Sandstone Bed of the Chinle Formation in Navajo County, Arizona.
Pravusuchus belongs to the parent group Leptosuchomorpha.
It is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Pravusuchus is the sister taxon to the Mystriosuchini clade.
Pravusuchus is considered more evolutionarily derived than the genera Leptosuchus and Smilosuchus.
Pravusuchus lived during the Late Triassic (Norian stage) in Arizona, United States.
The animal lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
